{{Short description|Russian pianist and biologist (born 1936)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2026}}

'''Galina Dmitrievna Shostakovich''' ({{langx|ru|Галина Дмитриевна Шостакович}}; born in [[Saint Petersburg|Leningrad]] on 30 May 1936) is a Russian trained pianist and biologist.

== Early life ==
She is the sister of [[Maxim Shostakovich]] (born 1938) and the first child of [[Dmitri Shostakovich]] and physicist Nina Vasilyevna Varzar.

She received early training on the piano from her father. She is the dedicatee of his ''[[Children's Notebook]]'', [[Opus number|Op]]. 69, which was composed for her ninth birthday on 30 May 1945. She wanted to become a ballerina. She learned several languages. At age 11 her French already was as good as her Russian.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kp.ru/daily/26084.4/2986721/|title=В дачном поселке Жуковка по Рублевскому шоссе первым бассейн построил Ростропович|first=Анастасия ПЛЕШАКОВА &#124; Сайт «Комсомольской|last=правды»|date=30 May 2013|publisher=}}</ref> She started studying composition with her father at an early age. Soon after the death of her mother Nina Vasilyevna Varzar (born in 1909) on 4 December 1954, Galina Shostakovich enrolled in Biology at the [[Moscow University]] where she graduated in 1959. In 1959 she married Yevgeniy Borisovich Chukovsky (1937–1997), a cinematographer and cameraman. He was the grandson of author and children's poet [[Korney Chukovsky]] and nephew of [[Lidiya Chukovskaya]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Ivashkin|first1=Alexander|last2=Kirkman|first2=Andrew|title=Contemplating Shostakovich: Life, Music and Film|year=2012|publisher=Ashgate|isbn=978-1-4094-3937-0|pages=314}}</ref>

In a letter to his daughter on 6 August 1958, her father told her: "...Time goes by. And love in life – this is the most important thing. Besides this, it is very serious and responsible. There should always be a harmonious combination of the senses and the intellect. I really want to see your life was good, so that you are always healthy and happy. Kiss you. Dad."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://live.shostakovich.or.multimedia.ru/chronicle/year-1958/|title=Дмитрий Шостакович Биография|publisher=|access-date=12 October 2015|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304122144/http://live.shostakovich.or.multimedia.ru/chronicle/year-1958/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Her first son Andrei was born in August 1960 and her second son Nikolai in January 1962.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Wilson|first1=Elisabeth|title=Shostakovich: A Life Remembered|date=2006|publisher=Princeton University Press|isbn=9780691128863|pages=600}}</ref>

== Career ==
She is interviewed in the documentary from 1997 ''The War Symphonies: Shostakovich Against Stalin'' by [[Larry Weinstein]] released on 10 May 2003.{{citation needed|date=July 2021}}
